A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Ego-Foresight work and provide readable text, equations, figures, and results. All supplied pages were inspected, including v4 Appendix A.1–A.5. v3 ends after its references and contains no appendix.

before.justification: v3 reports original DrQv2-EF experiments, hyperparameter ablations, and qualitative predictions on simulated tasks and the real-world BAIR dataset.

after.justification: v4 reports original DrQv2-EF and TD-MPC2-EF experiments, ablations, and feature analyses. BAIR prediction results remain in Appendix A.2, although some benchmark baseline results are explicitly reused from their authors.

M1.justification: v3 implements EF with DrQ-v2 and leaves model-based integration as future work. v4 implements TD-MPC2-EF, sharing its visual encoder and adding EF modules and reconstruction loss to the world-model objective (Section 3.3, Equation 7). The underlying EF disentanglement mechanism and DrQ-v2 integration remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: The distracting-background and hurdle-obstacle DMC evaluations in v3 are replaced by ten standard DMC tasks in v4, including Acrobot Swingup and Finger Turn Hard. This changes both task coverage and environmental conditions. The same sixteen Meta-World tasks and BAIR dataset remain; BAIR moves to Appendix A.2.

E2.justification: v3 compares DrQv2-EF with DrQ-v2, SEAR, and Dreamer-v3. v4 adds CURL to the Meta-World and DMC learning-curve comparisons and evaluates TD-MPC2 against TD-MPC2-EF on DMC. CURL is absent from the new Rliable Figure 7 despite the accompanying prose claiming a comparison there.

E3.justification: v4 adds best-evaluation-score aggregation using median, interquartile mean, and mean, plus a controlled throughput evaluation. New TD-MPC2-EF experiments use 512-dimensional features and 1,250 babbling steps. Meta-World tool-task aggregation expands from seven to eight tasks by including Basketball. The existing threshold-based aggregate calculation is retained and named ENS.

E4.justification: v4 removes the distracting-background and hurdle stress evaluations, including evidence of weaknesses under visual distractions. It adds computational-cost analysis and Hammer feature visualizations with thresholded-mask precision and recall (Appendices A.4–A.5). Figure 4 extends displayed predictions from step 18 to step 28. The four original hyperparameter ablations and BAIR examples are retained.

E5.justification: v3 reports five-seed means and standard deviations. v4 adds aggregate error bars and median, interquartile-mean, and mean estimates with 95% stratified bootstrap confidence intervals (Figure 7). It retains the five-seed convention while explicitly identifying three available seeds for the new TD-MPC2 baseline on DMC; this does not establish increased runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: v4 adds standard-DMC results, CURL comparisons, TD-MPC2-EF results reporting improvement on eight of ten tasks, aggregate statistical estimates, throughput measurements, and Hammer mask-overlap scores. Distracting/Hurdle results disappear. The reported DrQv2-EF improvement count changes from 17/25 to 21/26 tasks, but these counts concern different evaluation coverage and cannot establish a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: v4 adds a formal definition of the TD-MPC2-EF objective in Equation 7, supported by TD-MPC2 component and loss definitions in Equations 3–4. Existing Bellman and EF reconstruction mathematics is substantially unchanged apart from notation and clarification. Neither version contains theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion expand the demonstrated contribution from extending one model-free algorithm to extending both DrQ-v2 and model-based TD-MPC2. Model-based integration changes from future work to a delivered contribution. Real-world unseen-trajectory prediction is no longer highlighted in the contribution list, although its evidence remains in the appendix.

C2.justification: v3's specific explanations for poor Distracting DMC performance are removed, while the general pixel-reconstruction limitation remains. v4 adds interpretations concerning applicability across RL architectures, competition between agent and scene representation capacity, and blur from predictions beyond the training horizon. Appendix A.5 qualifies its mask-overlap measurements as sensitive to patch size and threshold.

D1.justification: v4 adds TD-MPC2-specific settings, hardware and timing information, and identifies reused official DMC baseline results (Appendices A.1 and A.4). Much of the original architecture documentation is relocated. Conversely, v3's explicit default loss weight of 1 and three context frames are omitted, and its direct code-access link is replaced by a media link; external resource availability cannot be established.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations supporting bootstrap evaluation, reconstruction limitations, and temporal contrastive learning, including Agarwal et al., Hansen et al. (2022), LeCun, and Zheng et al. It removes several robotics references, including Wilkins and Stathis and the controllable-point discussion. Most positioning is retained, while TD-MPC2 becomes an implemented parent algorithm rather than only background.

P1.justification: v4 separates Background from Related Work, moves Related Work after the experiments, and relocates architecture and BAIR material into a new appendix. The abstract, contribution list, integration explanation, experimental narrative, and conclusion are substantially revised. The publication template and author/header presentation also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned and regrouped; Meta-World plots are split into tool and non-tool tasks; new DMC curves are separated by algorithm family. BAIR panels become separate appendix figures, and trajectory displays are rearranged and extended. Rliable Figure 7, feature-analysis Figure 13, and two tables add substantial new displays within a changed page layout.

improvement.justification: The implemented TD-MPC2 extension supplies evidence for applicability that v3 left as future work. CURL comparisons, bootstrap uncertainty, and measured computational costs also strengthen evaluation and transparency. These gains are tempered by removing the challenging DMC tests and their documented failures, omitting explicit reproducibility defaults, and claiming a Rliable comparison with CURL that Figure 7 does not show. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
